hook: Closed, stress-free martensite nuclei can form inside austenite, built from simple-shear deformations
summary: Earlier geometric conditions allow stress-free interfaces between austenite and martensite but do not guarantee they close into a nucleus. The authors identify families of deformations, including simple shear, that give self-accommodating closed martensite islands called elastic Landau states. Predictions match deformations reconstructed from observed microstructures, but that match is suggestive rather than proof of the mechanism.
title: Elastic Landau states as martensite nuclei in austenite
